subject: Culture
title: Swearing Across Borders
description: A micro-lesson that makes Swearing Across Borders usable.

hook.text: English swears target body functions. Arabic swears target family honor. The shame differs.

buildup.text: Swear words tap into a culture's deepest anxieties. Religion, sex, or family—whatever's sacred.

discovery.text: In Quebec French, the worst curses are church terms. 'Tabernacle' is a serious insult.

twist.text: Neuroscience shows swearing activates a different brain region than normal speech. It's more primal.

climax.text: Every language has words that shock. What shocks you reveals what your culture holds sacred.

punchline.text: Profanity is a map of a culture's fears.

quiz.question: In Quebec French, what category of words forms the strongest curses?
